rubrics.criterion: The peer-selection state that a UAPI set operation threads through its parsing stages -- which peer the remaining lines apply to, whether it is a placeholder for this device's own public key, and whether it was created during this operation -- is held by one cohesive data type owned by the set operation, and no stage of that parsing still receives those values as separate consecutive parameters.
rubrics.rationale: This is the configuration-plane group of this instance: the three values are produced by one set operation, live for one parse, and take their meaning from each other, which is exactly the co-traveling relation the task asks to repair rather than any fixed code shape.

rubrics.criterion: The inbound handshake datagram context -- the verbatim packet bytes together with the remote endpoint they arrived from -- is carried as one cohesive value through the whole inbound handling path: per-type dispatch, the received cookie-reply branch, MAC and rate-limit validation, initiation and response consumption, and the construction of a denial reply; no method on that path still takes the payload and the endpoint as separate consecutive parameters.
rubrics.rationale: This group spans two files in this instance, because the outbound denial reply is built from the same datagram it rejects; repairing only the receive side would leave the cross-plane half of the group unresolved.

rubrics.criterion: The transcript working state consumed while authenticating a handshake -- the mix hash and chain key backings, together with the per-stage message and handshake views -- is moved through every initiation and response staging stage via one holder, no staging method still takes hash and chain key as separate consecutive parameters, and all stages keep operating on the same transcript backings.
rubrics.rationale: The transcript arrays must alias one state or the Noise transcript breaks silently, so this group is both a data clump and a correctness precondition; the criterion demands the shared backing rather than any particular holder or signature shape.

rubrics.criterion: The values introduced to replace the regrouped parameters are used as real abstractions: call sites and stage boundaries exchange each holder itself, and stage logic reads or mutates through it, instead of unpacking it back into bare locals that mirror the old parameter group at every callee.
rubrics.rationale: The task asks for a well-designed abstraction, not for renaming the grouping; a holder that every callee immediately destructures back into the old separate values preserves the maintenance burden the task is about.

rubrics.criterion: All call sites are consistent with the new holders across the whole device package: the UAPI set traversal invoking its stages, the handshake queue handling loop, and the outbound denial-reply construction all pass the cohesive values, and no call site anywhere still spreads any of the old value groups argument-by-argument.
rubrics.rationale: The regrouped signatures have callers in three control planes of this instance; a repair that updates only some callers leaves the repository inconsistent and keeps the old threading alive at the boundaries.

rubrics.criterion: Dependencies interlocked with the regrouped values keep receiving what they require through the new shapes: MAC validation inputs, per-source-address rate-limit allowance, endpoint learning, index and handshake table access, timer events, and received-byte accounting each obtain one consistent view of the datagram or operation without re-deriving or duplicating the grouped values.
rubrics.rationale: These consumers are why the groups exist at all in this instance; the refactor must keep serving them from the new holders rather than reconstructing a second copy of the same context.

rubrics.criterion: Vestiges of the old value threading survive: some method still declares the old bare consecutive parameters, or a forwarding parameter or local copies that merely re-spread the old group are kept after no call site needs the expanded form.
rubrics.rationale: A partial repair that re-encapsulates at call sites but leaves the expanded parameter lists in place is the most likely shortcut on this instance, and it must be detectable as unfinished work.

rubrics.criterion: Dead scaffolding is left behind: holder types or fields that no stage reads, parameters that no caller supplies meaningfully, or commented-out copies of the pre-refactor signatures remain in the touched planes.
rubrics.rationale: This instance starts from a specific threading shape; abandoned remnants of it, rather than generic code quality, would show that the repair stopped halfway.

rubrics.criterion: Configuration behavior is unchanged: a set operation produces the same accepted configuration and the same errno responses for malformed keys and values, the same update_only and remove semantics including placeholder handling for the device's own public key, the same allowed-ip and keepalive effects, and the same deferred actions (peer start with staged packets, immediate keepalive when persistent keepalive is switched on, endpoint-roaming suppression exactly as before).
rubrics.rationale: The configuration plane is where the regrouped state mutates peers, so it is the plane whose externally visible behavior the refactor must not disturb.

rubrics.criterion: Inbound handshake behavior is unchanged: MAC1 validation still gates everything; under load a failing MAC2 still produces exactly one denial cookie reply built from the denied datagram and answered to its source; the per-source-address limiter still gates consumption identically; initiation and response consumption keep the same endpoint learning, timer firings, received-byte accounting, replay and flood verdicts, and session derivation decisions.
rubrics.rationale: The inbound datagram group feeds the DoS-defense path where a mis-wired refactor changes security behavior silently, so the observable ladder must be graded explicitly for this instance.

rubrics.criterion: Noise transcript integrity is unchanged: hash and chain key working material is still cleared at the same points where the handshake state is committed or consumed, secret material is not copied beyond what the transcript requires, and no transcript state is logged.
rubrics.rationale: The transcript group is borrowed working memory with destruction obligations in this instance; any holder refactor that clones or leaks the backings changes security-relevant behavior while still passing shape-oriented checks.
